newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Pacific Capital Assets to seek NZSE listing.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Pacific Capital Assets to seek NZSE listing.

text.p: Pacific Capital Assets Ltd, the proposed parent company of Britomart Investments, confirmed on Monday that it intended to seek a listing on the New Zealand Stock Exchange.
Pacific Capital said the listing would allow investors to participate in the Britomart project in downtown Auckland by taking up shares in a public pool.
A lead manager for the offer is expected to be appointed soon and details of the timing and size of the float would be announced over the coming weeks, Pacific Capital said.
The float would be fully underwritten.
Pacific Capital is an investment holding company intending to specialise in infrastructure-related development projects.
The company said it was backed by a consortium of investors based in Australia and Asia, including Hudson Corporate Pty Ltd, Idris Hydraulic (Malaysia) Berhad and First KL Group.
"The Britomart project is the first of a number of infrastructure-related projects with which the company is likely to become involved," Pacific Capital said.
Hudson Corporate is part of Australia's Hudson Timber and Hardware, whose major shareholders are from Singapore and Malaysia.
Britomart Investments and Britomart Developments Ltd had been set up as special purpose companies last year to undertake the Britomart project.

The companies had been nominated by NatWest Markets Australia as the developers for Britomart under the terms of NatWest's contract with Auckland City, subject to that contract becoming unconditional.
NatWest is a unit of National Westminster Bank.
Pacific Capital Assets would provide substantial equity for the project and undertake above ground development.
Bob Challinor, a director of Electricity Corp of New Zealand, had been appointed chairman.
Challinor is also a director of Moana Pacific Fisheries, National Insurance and Health (chairman), Sheffield Consulting Group and The Warehouse.

Auckland-based Bruce Davidson had been appointed as an independent director. Other board members are: Datuk Haji Ishak Ismail, Tsang Jat Meng, Albert Cheok, David Atkin and Jihong Lu (managing director).
No further details were available, but newspapers have speculated the issue would total NZ$50 million.
The Britomart project is estimated to cost NZ$1.5 billion, including above ground development of medium-rise apartments, commercial offices, hotels and shops.
